title: Jarom Writes
summary: Jarom writes a few words on the plates according to Enos’s commandment, to preserve their genealogy.

explicit_facts.text: Jarom writes a few words according to the commandment of his father, Enos, so that their genealogy may be kept.

unspecified_visual_details: Jarom’s age, clothing, and appearance; the writing tools and surroundings.

narration.text: Now behold, I, Jarom, write a few words

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Enos as present; the verse mentions him but does not place him in the scene.

title: A Brief Record
summary: Jarom explains that the plates are small and that he will write only a little, not his prophecies or revelations.

explicit_facts.text: Jarom says the plates are small and that he will write a little for the benefit of their Lamanite brethren, omitting his prophecies and revelations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jarom may be shown continuing to write on the plates.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the plates, writing tools, and surroundings.

narration.text: as these plates are small
I shall not write the things of my prophesying, nor of my revelations.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse refers to earlier writings about the plan of salvation; it does not narrate those writings as a visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Jarom’s prophecies or revelations as visible events.

title: A People in Need
summary: Jarom describes the people’s hardness of heart and God’s mercy in not yet sweeping them from the land.

explicit_facts.text: Jarom says much must be done among the people because of their hardness, deafness, blindness, and stiffness; God is merciful and has not yet swept them from the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jarom may be shown writing as he reflects on the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities, individual appearance, and any specific setting.

narration.text: God is exceedingly merciful unto them
has not as yet swept them off from the face of the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The descriptions of deafness, blindness, and stiff necks are figures of speech, not literal visible conditions.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine intervention or destruction; neither is narrated as occurring.

title: Faith and Revelation
summary: Jarom says many among the people receive revelations, and those who have faith commune with the Holy Spirit.

explicit_facts.text: Jarom says many among the people have revelations; those who are not stiffnecked and have faith have communion with the Holy Spirit.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jarom may be shown writing this account.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of those who receive revelations; how communion with the Holy Spirit is visually manifested.

narration.text: many among us who have many revelations
have communion with the Holy Spirit

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes spiritual communion, but does not describe a visible appearance of the Holy Spirit.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible manifestation of the Holy Spirit or depict a specific revelation.

title: The Nephites at Two Hundred Years
summary: Two hundred years have passed; the Nephites are strong, observe the law of Moses and the sabbath, and have strict laws.

explicit_facts.text: Two hundred years have passed, and the people of Nephi have grown strong in the land.
They observe the law of Moses and keep the sabbath day holy; they do not profane or blaspheme, and the laws of the land are exceedingly strict.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A community of Nephites may be shown in their land.
unspecified_visual_details: The community’s architecture, clothing, specific sabbath observances, and the content or enforcement of the laws.

narration.text: the people of Nephi had waxed strong in the land.
They observed to keep the law of Moses and the sabbath day holy unto the Lord.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a particular ritual, law, or legal proceeding.

title: Peoples Across the Land
summary: Nephites and Lamanites are scattered across much of the land; the Lamanites are more numerous.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites and Lamanites are scattered across much of the land; the Lamanites greatly outnumber the Nephites.
Jarom says the Lamanites love murder and drink the blood of beasts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two peoples may be shown in separate areas of a broad landscape to suggest their distribution.
unspecified_visual_details: Their precise locations, appearance, and the circumstances of the reported practices.

narration.text: the Lamanites also
they were exceedingly more numerous than were they of the Nephites

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports the Lamanites’ practices; it does not narrate a specific murder or drinking event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a particular murder, victim, or blood-drinking act.

title: Battles and Fortifications
summary: Lamanites come against the Nephites many times; Nephite leaders teach the people, the Nephites withstand the attacks, and they begin fortifying their cities and inherited lands.

explicit_facts.text: The Lamanites come against the Nephites many times to battle; Nephite kings and leaders are mighty in faith and teach the people the ways of the Lord.
The Nephites withstand the Lamanites and drive them out of their lands, then begin fortifying their cities or other places of inheritance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A battle between the groups and construction of fortifications are described, but as recurring and subsequent actions; keep them in separate visual moments.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific battles, leaders’ identities, weapons, city designs, and the exact place fortified.

narration.text: they came many times against us, the Nephites, to battle.
we withstood the Lamanites and swept them away out of our lands

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse summarizes repeated battles and does not identify a particular battle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not merge multiple battles into one specific event or invent named leaders.

title: Nephite Prosperity and Preparation
summary: The Nephites multiply and spread, become rich, and make tools and weapons as preparations for war.

explicit_facts.text: The Nephites multiply, spread across the land, and become rich in precious materials and workmanship.
They make tools for tilling the ground and weapons of war, including arrows, quivers, darts, and javelins.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephites may be shown making tools and weapons from the listed materials.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific buildings, machinery, designs, work methods, and the appearance of the people.

narration.text: we multiplied exceedingly, and spread upon the face of the land
all preparations for war.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a specific workshop, battle, or weapon beyond those named.

title: Prepared in the Land
summary: The Nephites are prepared to meet the Lamanites, who do not prosper against them; Jarom recalls the Lord’s promise of prosperity for commandment keeping.

explicit_facts.text: Prepared to meet the Lamanites, the Nephites do not suffer the Lamanites to prosper against them.
The word of the Lord to their fathers is verified: keeping the commandments brings prosperity in the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Nephites may be shown prepared for defense, without depicting a specific battle.
unspecified_visual_details: The particular encounter, defensive preparations, and appearance of the people.

narration.text: they did not prosper against us.
Inasmuch as ye will keep my commandments ye shall prosper in the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The quoted promise is recalled by Jarom; it is not a new spoken scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a new divine appearance or a specific battle not narrated.

title: The Prophets Warn
summary: The Lord’s prophets warn the Nephites that transgression will lead to their destruction from the land.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord’s prophets threaten the Nephites according to God’s word: if they transgress rather than keep the commandments, they will be destroyed from the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The warning may be conveyed as off-screen narration over a supported setting, without depicting the predicted destruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The prophets’ identities, number, appearance, and the setting of their warning.

narration.text: if they did not keep the commandments
they should be destroyed from off the face of the land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The destruction is conditional and predicted, not an event occurring in this verse.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the predicted destruction happening.

title: Teaching the People
summary: Prophets, priests, and teachers labor diligently, teaching the law of Moses and persuading the people to look forward to the Messiah.

explicit_facts.text: Prophets, priests, and teachers diligently exhort the people, teach the law of Moses and its purpose, and persuade them to look forward to the Messiah and believe in him to come as though he already was.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A teacher may be shown addressing listeners; the verse does not identify a particular speaker.
unspecified_visual_details: The individuals’ identities, appearance, gathering place, and the form of their teaching.

narration.text: teaching the law of Moses, and the intent for which it was given
persuading them to look forward unto the Messiah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Messiah is referred to as one to come; no appearance or visible event is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Messiah as present.

title: Stirred to Repentance
summary: Through this teaching, the people are kept from destruction and continually stirred to repentance.

explicit_facts.text: By the teachers’ efforts, the Nephites are kept from destruction; the word continually pricks their hearts and stirs them to repentance.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching may be represented through a supported setting with narration rather than inventing a particular conversion event.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s individual responses and any specific occasion of repentance.

narration.text: they did prick their hearts with the word
continually stirring them up unto repentance.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Prick their hearts” is figurative language, not a literal injury.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal wounds or a single specific conversion.

title: Wars and Contentions
summary: By the passing of 238 years, wars, contentions, and dissensions have occupied much of the time.

explicit_facts.text: Two hundred thirty-eight years have passed, with wars, contentions, and dissensions for much of the time.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jarom may be shown writing a summary of the passage of time.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific conflicts, participants, dates, and places.

narration.text: two hundred and thirty and eight years had passed away
wars, and contentions, and dissensions

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This verse summarizes extended conditions; it does not specify a distinct battle to depict.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a particular war or conflict scene.

title: The Plates Passed to Omni
summary: Jarom says he will write no more, directs his brethren to Nephi’s other plates for records of wars, and gives his plates to his son Omni to keep.

explicit_facts.text: Jarom says the plates are small and directs his brethren to the other plates of Nephi for records of wars.
Jarom delivers the plates to his son Omni to be kept according to the commandments of his fathers.

unspecified_visual_details: The location, the plates’ appearance, and the ages and appearances of Jarom and Omni.

narration.text: I deliver these plates into the hands of my son Omni

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the other plates or the wars recorded on them as present events.
